source_caption:
To secure the green light for an incredibly ambitious, fiercely anti-war animated feature, director Brad Bird pitched the studio a single, profoundly devastating premise: what if a gun had a soul, and it chose not to be a weapon? To voice the massive, deeply destructive alien machine, Bird cast a then-unknown Vin Diesel, utilizing his naturally deep, gravelly register to convey immense physical weight. However, during the film’s utterly shattering climax, as the giant intercepts a nuclear missile to save the town, Diesel was required to deliver the single word Superman. Behind the scenes, the actor became so intensely overwhelmed by the emotional weight of a living weapon actively choosing to be a hero that he actually broke down in tears in the recording booth. By stripping away all robotic modulation for that final, profoundly human utterance, Diesel masterfully proves that the most devastating cinematic sacrifices do not require grand, sweeping speeches, but simply the quiet, unshakeable courage to finally choose who you want to be.
⠀
The Iron Giant (1999), directed by Brad Bird, starring Eli Marienthal, Vin Diesel, Jennifer Aniston. During the deeply paranoid, heavily militarized height of the Cold War, a fiercely imaginative young boy discovers a massive, amnesiac alien robot in the woods, sparking a profoundly beautiful friendship that is violently threatened by a terrified, highly aggressive government agent determined to destroy what he cannot understand.

source_details.title: The Iron Giant
source_details.synopsis: The Iron Giant is a 1999 American animated science fiction film directed by Brad Bird (in his feature directorial debut) and written by Tim McCanlies. Loosely based on Ted Hughes's 1968 novel The Iron Man, it features an ensemble cast consisting of Jennifer Aniston, Harry Connick Jr., Vin Diesel, James Gammon, Cloris Leachman, John Mahoney, Eli Marienthal, Christopher McDonald and M. Emmet Walsh. Set during the Cold War in 1957, the film centers on a young boy named Hogarth Hughes, who discovers and befriends a giant robot of extraterrestrial origin.
